text.p: Italian Btp bond futures closed strongly firmer after touching a new high of 135.58 in the session and 135.60 in Liffe APT trading, boosted by a rally in U.S. Treasuries which lifted Bund futures and other debt markets. The Bund spread earlier narrowed to a 103 bp low.

Dealers said they had no fixed goals for the September Btp after it continued to explore new higher ground after breaking up through chart points at 135.40 and 135.50, and said they were instead watching targets on the 10-year Bund spread.
"Levels of 100 basis points for the spread over Germany and 35 bps for Spain are just round the corner," one said.
"Perhaps we will see some profit-taking when the market reaches the spread targets but for the moment there's no sign of a correction in sight," one operator said.
T-bonds and Bund futures surged after news of only a modest rise in U.S. payrolls eased fears of wage-driven inflation and came after the FOMC left Fed Funds rates alone.
The U.S. is on holiday on Friday.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 rose 50 bps to 101.42 yielding 6.64 percent.
"If Bunds continue to rise the the Btp will follow," one trader said.

On the interbank market, today's Bank of Italy 7.5 trillion lire repo, which saw a minimum rate of 6.83 percent, disappointed some treasury managers who had expected an operation of a higher amount and caused money rates to rise slightly.
The average overnight rate was 6.97 percent against 6.91 on Wednesday while tomorrow/next was at 6.98 against 6.96 and spot/next at 6.97 versus 6.96.
